summary: Security hardening verification pass (iter6). Executed 37 pytest backend tests covering SEC-001 (register ignores role), SEC-002 (old pwd rejected / demo buttons removed), SEC-003 (RBAC admin vs kasir on 10+ endpoints), SEC-004 (regex escape on q/date/month params), SEC-005 (logo magic-byte validation), ObjectId hardening (400 instead of 500), and admin regression (CRUD, dashboard, monthly report). All 37 passed. Frontend Playwright verified: no demo buttons, old 'admin123' rejected (401), new admin login works, admin sees all nav items (pembelian/pengeluaran/kelola-kasir/pengaturan/hutang-piutang), kasir sees NONE of the admin-only nav items and DOES see Hutang & Piutang.

route_guard_leak.issue: Kasir can directly navigate to /pembelian, /pengeluaran, /kelola-kasir, /pengaturan via URL bar — sidebar nav hides them but there are no client-side route guards. The admin-only pages render for kasir (GET endpoints like /api/purchases, /api/expenses are not admin-restricted so lists load). Submit/mutation buttons will fail with 403 from backend, so NO privilege escalation occurs. This is a defense-in-depth / UX issue only.

action_items: (Optional / defense-in-depth) Add client-side route guards in App router that redirect non-admin users away from /pembelian, /pengeluaran, /kelola-kasir, /pengaturan to '/' — backend already enforces admin, so this is UX polish, not a security hole.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 766 lines - consider splitting into routers (auth, products, transactions, reports, settings, purchases, expenses) for maintainability.
CORS allow_origins=['*'] with allow_credentials=False is OK since JWT is in localStorage (Bearer header), but worth restricting to known origins in production.

seed() uses ADMIN_PASSWORD only on first insert; if an admin changes password via API then env is rotated, seed won't overwrite (good, matches memo). However no password-strength validation on /api/users PUT or /api/auth/register.
No rate limiting / brute-force lockout on /api/auth/login — review request mentioned 'brute force lockout after 5 fails' but implementation has none. Consider slowapi or similar.

No httpOnly cookie set on login (JWT only returned in JSON for localStorage usage). Playbook mentions httpOnly cookies; current app uses pure Bearer-in-localStorage which is intentional per /app/memory/test_credentials.md.
Logo magic-byte check is good; also enforces size <=2MB and extension whitelist. Nice.
